documents.title: Office Visit - palpitations, weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: "my heart races and I'm losing weight without trying."

HPI: 68 y/o with HTN on HCTZ booked this herself. Since around the start of the year she has noticed her heart pounding or fluttering, mostly when sitting quietly in the evening, lasting minutes to longer, no fainting. Feels warm when others are comfortable, sleeps with the window open. Eating more than usual, yet clothes are looser. Bowels moving more often than they used to, formed, not diarrhea. No chest pain, no shortness of breath at rest. No neck pain. No new medicines or supplements, no iodine contrast, no biotin.
Sister has Graves disease and she wondered about that herself.

Weight today 55 kg; 58 kg at her wellness visit last September.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: pulse 104 and regular at rooming, 98 on the ECG a few minutes later. Afebrile. Thin, comfortable. Eyes: no proptosis, no lid lag that I can appreciate. Neck nontender. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.

ECG in office: sinus rhythm 98, no other abnormality.

Assessment: her symptoms strongly suggest hyperthyroidism, Graves likely given family history. Unintentional weight loss of 3 kg.
Plan:
- TSH now; I'll call with the result. If suppressed, urgent endocrinology referral.
- Return/ED precautions reviewed: chest pain, fainting, heart rate that stays very fast or irregular, shortness of breath.
- Bone health: overactive thyroid adds to her bone risk on top of early menopause, mother's hip fracture and years of little dietary calcium. Raised the DXA again and this time she agrees. Ordered.

Primary care

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text:
Indication: postmenopausal woman, early menopause, family history of hip fracture, suspected hyperthyroidism. Technique: DXA of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. No prior study for comparison. All four lumbar vertebrae evaluable, no artifact excluded.
Lumbar spine L1-L4: T-score -2.8.
Left femoral neck: T-score -2.7.
reports.conclusion: Bone mineral density in the osteoporotic range by WHO criteria at the lumbar spine and left femoral neck. Baseline study.

events.reason: DXA result; calcium and vitamin D

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (600 mg) by mouth three times daily with meals (over the counter)
Take 1 capsule (2000 units) by mouth daily

documents.title: Your bone density result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Sandra,

Your bone density scan shows osteoporosis: T-score -2.8 at the lower spine and -2.7 at the hip (anything at or below -2.5 is in that range). Early menopause, your mother's history and a lifetime with little dairy all play a part, and the overactive thyroid likely adds to it.

Two things to start now, both over the counter:
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg, one tablet with each meal (three a day). With food it absorbs better.
- Vitamin D3 2000 units once a day.

There are prescription medicines that lower fracture risk, and I'd like to go over them with you. No rush this week with the thyroid appointment coming up.

Your PCP

documents.body: Thank you. I'll pick up the calcium and vitamin D tomorrow. Could we talk about the bone medicines after I see the thyroid doctor? One thing at a time. I've read some scary things about those drugs.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/20/2021
Referred by: primary care, for suppressed TSH

Thank you for sending Ms. Walsh, a 68-year-old woman with hypertension and newly found osteoporosis.

History: For roughly half a year she has had episodes of a racing heartbeat, intolerance of warm rooms, and a weight drop despite eating more. Bowel movements have become more frequent though not loose. No eye irritation, double vision or neck pain. No recent iodine load, no amiodarone, no biotin.

Past history: hypertension; mild bilateral knee osteoarthritis; osteoporosis on DXA 7/13/21 (L1-L4 -2.8, femoral neck -2.7); menopause at 45, no HRT; lactose intolerance. Surgery: left cataract with IOL.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg TID with meals; cholecalciferol 2000 units daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: sister with Graves disease; father with atrial fibrillation and hypertension; mother with hypertension and osteoporotic hip fracture at 82; maternal grandmother with rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: never smoker; wine socially, 1-2 glasses a week, with periods of none. Semi-retired, works from home.

Exam: HR 102, BP 138/86, weight 55 kg. Fine tremor with arms outstretched. Skin warm and moist. Thyroid diffusely enlarged, smooth, not tender, no nodules, no bruit. No proptosis or lid retraction. Heart irregularly irregular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Data:
TSH <0.01 mIU/L (0.4-4.0)
Free T4 3.2 ng/dL (0.8-1.8)
Calcium 10.2 mg/dL (8.5-10.2)
Alkaline phosphatase 150 U/L (30-120)
Transaminases, bilirubin, albumin normal; CBC normal (baseline before antithyroid drug).
ECG today: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Her ECG at your office on 7/6 was sinus.

Assessment:
1. Graves disease: overt hyperthyroidism with a diffuse nontender goiter, fine tremor and a sister with the same diagnosis. The alkaline phosphatase and high-normal calcium fit increased bone turnover from thyrotoxicosis.
2. Atrial fibrillation with RVR, paroxysmal, driven by thyrotoxicosis.
3. Osteoporosis, with thyrotoxicosis a contributor.

Plan:
- Methimazole 10 mg daily. Reviewed agranulocytosis warning (stop and call for fever or sore throat) and liver symptoms. Baseline CBC and liver tests done today.
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily for rate and symptom control.
- Repeat free T4 and TSH with ECG at follow-up in about 8 weeks.
- Continue HCTZ, calcium and vitamin D as prescribed by you.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Office Visit - osteoporosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to talk through bone protection, about three months after her first endocrinology visit for Graves.

S: Nothing acute. Feels well. Admits she's been less active the last few years as her consulting work tapered off. No pain at rest. Stiff when she first gets out of bed, and thinks she walks a bit slower than she used to. Knees: the same mild arthritis, nothing new. Never fallen, never broken a bone. ROS negative for weakness, numbness and any recent weight change (weight steady since summer). Palpitations gone off metoprolol.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily (her only BP medicine); methimazole 10 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg TID with meals; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
NKDA. Never smoker, occasional glass of wine.

O: Vitals normal (flowsheet). Well appearing. Spine without tenderness. Strength 5/5 in hips and legs, rises from chair without hands. Gait steady, normal tandem walk. Knees mild crepitus, no effusion.

DXA 7/13/21 reviewed with her: L1-L4 T -2.8, femoral neck T -2.7.

A/P: Osteoporosis, postmenopausal, risk factors early menopause, maternal hip fracture, long low calcium intake, recent thyrotoxicosis.
We went through options: weekly alendronate, a yearly zoledronic acid infusion, and denosumab injections every 6 months, with how much each lowers fracture risk and the side effects she has read about (jaw osteonecrosis, unusual thigh fractures, stomach upset). She would rather not take a bone drug now - the side effects worry her and she wants to give the non-drug approach a fair try first, and let the thyroid settle. Her choice; she knows she can revisit any time.
- Continue calcium carbonate 600 mg TID and D3 2000 units.
- Weight-bearing exercise: daily brisk walking, add simple balance and leg-strength work (handout).
- Fall prevention at home: lighting on stairs, nonslip mat, shoes with grip outdoors.
- Getting the Graves under control will help her bones.
HTN on HCTZ controlled. Next visit March.

documents.title: Office Visit - fatigue, back discomfort
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
69 y/o with osteoporosis, Graves (euthyroid on methimazole), HTN, back about a year after our bone-health talk.

S: Over the past year she has felt steadily more tired, and has a mild ache across the middle of her back. She puts both down to getting older and to hunching over the laptop at her kitchen-table desk. No focal weakness, no pins and needles, no real joint pain beyond the usual knee stiffness. Still walks every day. She has the sense she's gotten shorter and her trousers sit differently at the waist.
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, change in bowels or bladder. No palpitations or heat intolerance.
Diet: still avoids dairy - lactose intolerance - so her calcium is from the tablets.
Menopause at 45, never on HRT.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily; methimazole 10 daily; calcium carbonate 600 TID; D3 2000 units daily. NKDA.

O: BP 132/78, P 76, SpO2 98%. Wt 54 kg, Ht 160 cm, BMI 21.1.
Her height in the 2017 records from her prior practice was 163 cm, and our own measurements ran 162.5 to 163.9 cm through 2021.
Mild thoracic kyphosis. No midline spinal tenderness to percussion. Paraspinals soft.
Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact to light touch, gait normal, Romberg negative.
Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, gradual - check CBC, BMP with calcium, TSH and free T4.
2. Mid-back discomfort with mild thoracic kyphosis and 3 cm loss of height, in a woman with osteoporosis. Neuro exam normal. Posture changes at her workstation (laptop riser, chair with lumbar support), keep walking daily, back extension exercises (handout, shown in the room).
3. Osteoporosis: calcium and vitamin D continue.
4. HTN: controlled on HCTZ.
Will message results.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sandra - good news, everything from yesterday is normal. Blood counts normal (no anemia), kidney function and calcium normal, and your thyroid levels are right where they should be on the methimazole. So nothing in the blood explains the tiredness. Let's see how you do with the walking, the desk changes and the back exercises, and let me know if things aren't improving. -PCP
